title: Kristen & Paisley:
title_short: Kristen & Paisley · They paid our mortgage
headline: Eight years after her daughter’s diagnosis, Kristen still remembers the day Family Reach paid their mortgage, and today Paisley is a thriving 11-year-old.
story: Kristen opens on the memory that stayed: Family Reach paid the mortgage. Then who she was, a working mom of two, and the day a sick visit turned into phone call after phone call, with the word “cancer” coming last.

Then the money: 44 days in the hospital, no way to earn. The hospital social workers bring up Family Reach, and one month without stress is the moment she remembers. Her point: families should not have to chase help. It ends on Paisley today, thriving, and “Because cancer is hard enough.” Warm and hopeful, never dark.

[00:50.6] We just did dinners and parties on the weekends and everything. And then as soon as the cancer diagnosis hit, I quit my job entirely. Our entire world's flipped upside down, and I was a stay-at-home mom at that point.
[01:02.3] Fast forward to now, I now have five children, three little ones. My daughter, Paisley, is 11. She's thriving in all aspects right now, and we're just one big happy family at this point.
[01:26.7] So I had brought Paisley into her pediatrician just for what I thought was some sort of illness, or maybe at one point, hand, foot, and mouth, or something along those lines.
[01:37.0] Come to find out it was petechiae down the road, but didn't think anything of just a typical sick visit at the pediatrician.

[02:20.3] She goes, I need you to go to Tufts Floating. More labs are coming back, and they're coming back not well. At this point, I still have not heard the word cancer. We're taken to Tufts Floating Hospital, the ER.
[02:30.3] They do more labs. They come in. They tell us it's either an immune deficiency, a blood infection, or cancer. And I think they're saying cancer just because they have to say cancer.

[03:08.9] But back then when you got the diagnosis information, that's all I could think of.

[03:58.3] And I am forever grateful for that because the relationship that I've made with the employees here and the help that I've received from them is something that I I couldn't be any more grateful for.

[04:35.1] I was receiving help from foundations and whatnot, but it was something that the social workers at the hospital were helping with, thank God, because I didn't have the time to put all my resources into chasing down all those leads and whatnot.
[04:48.1] We were stressed out every day about it, but it's something that I kind of put on the back burner and asked for help in situations like that for other people to take control for.

[06:47.0] Like I said, she was in the hospital for 44 days. I couldn't even physically leave the hospital to do anything to get any money.
